page.layout: One page of text, single column of verse; a Greek-heading line in the centre; catchword "GEOR-" at lower right; no margin notes.

main_text.p: Nec esse parili forte nos cognoscimus.
Nam maximum istud Iuppiter genuit malum,
main_text.head: E. GRÆCO.
main_text.p: PEnes tonantem est exitus rerum totem, Fili, arbitratu cuncta qui gerit suo.

p.i: At mens hominibus nulla momentaneis Est, in diemque viuitur mortalibus, Proui quidque numen singulis finuerit, Diuina blandis interim spes fomitis Fouet vniuersos vana volentes, diem Expectat ista cras tinum, ille plurimas Messes: nec vllus non sibi mortalium Promisit hilarémque & opulentum proximum Annum: sed aliúm tristis ante terminum Mors occupauit: morbus alium lugubris Extinguit: alios Martio in certamine Domitos nigrantes Pluto mittit ad domos: Aliis procellis aestuantis aequoris Iactans supremum claudit vnda spiritum, Quos vita curis tristis exercet malis Hi lacrimosa ad fata rete nexili Solis relinquunt sponte lumen. Sic mali Immune nihil est, mille sed mortalibus Parca minantur, ac inexplicabilis Dolor, & calamitas. Si mihi tribuant fidem, Se nullus vltro cruciet indulgens malis, Animum tenaci nec dolore exerceat.

page.notes: Greek heading "E. GRÆCO." is Latin lettering; the verse is Latin with some uncertain letters (e.g. "totem" as printed, "Pénes"/"Penes" initial P is a large initial). Some words in the scan are damaged and transcribed as best read; several spellings such as "finuerit", "fomitis", "nexili" are as printed. Left margin and right margin are free of notes.
